value.headline: Early voting surges in Kansas as voters weigh economy, key US Senate race that could break 94-year streak
value.claim: The number of Kansans voting early is about double this election compared to 2022's midterm.
value.evidence: KS SOS same-point comparison (via WIBW): 122,344 on 10/22/2026 vs 73,393 in 2022 = +66.7% (x1.67), not x2 [M from R]. NYT (via The Hill) +69%. The ratio was falling: Newsweek's 55,000 vs 27,000 (x2.05) used the 10/20 figure. vs 2018 same point 91,833: +33%. vs 2020 E-11: 154,074 vs 294,003 = -48% [V].

rows.source: KSHB 41 (Kansas City): Early voting surges in Kansas as voters weigh economy, key US Senate race that c
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: (same)
value.claim: Johnson County had 47,957 advance voters in the first three days vs 29,984 in 2022; Wyandotte 4,376 in four days vs 13,000 in all of 2022.
value.evidence: Not independently verified (county files not public in this run) [R]. Context [M]: Johnson County is 23.4% of Kansas registrants (Oct 1 2026) but its 47,957 is ~39% of the 122,344 statewide advance votes on 10/22: the early pool is geographically front-loaded toward the D-leaning KC suburbs (JoCo D 33.5% / R 39.4% registration vs state 25.7/44.5).

value.headline: Seven paragraphs to ponder as Kansas voters behold a blue wave gathering strength

value.evidence: Polls: Senate tied (raw D+1.0 minus fake firms; D+0.3 reweighted to 2024 recall), Governor R+4.7 raw / R+6.8 reweighted [M]. "Across Kansas" is not supported for the governor race or the House seats other than KS-03.
